hook.line: Every real-estate ad in Bogotá says the same thing: recién pintado, recién remodelado. The word *recién* tells you how fresh something is, and it's also how Latin Americans say they just arrived.
hook.en: The apartment has just been painted.

examples.en: The apartment has just been painted.
The walls have just been painted.

examples.es: Los recién casados se fueron a Cartagena.

rule:
*Recién* means just now. Put it before a participle and you get a fresh result: *recién pintado*, *recién hecho*, *recién llegado*.

The participle still agrees with what it describes: *el apartamento está recién pintado*, *las paredes están recién pintadas*.

Before a noun it can name people: *los recién casados* (the newlyweds), *un recién nacido* (a newborn).

Latin Americans also put *recién* before an ordinary past verb: *Recién llegué.* I just arrived. The preterite is the usual tense there.
smallPrint: Teachers call *recién* here an adverb of recent time; in Spain it appears only before participles.

options: The apartment has just been painted.
The wall has just been painted.
The walls have just been painted.
The bread was made a week ago.
I arrived a long time ago.
We've only just arrived in Bogotá.
I've only just arrived in Bogotá.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *pintado* or *pintada* and type the whole sentence: *La cocina está recién ___.* (The kitchen has just been painted.)
yourTurn.why: *Cocina* is feminine, so the participle ends in *-a*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *hecho* or *hecha* and type the whole sentence: *El pan está recién ___.* (The bread is freshly made.)
Say: The walls have just been painted.

yourTurn.why: With an ordinary verb, *recién* goes before the preterite.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: We've only just arrived in Bogotá.
Say: The coffee is freshly made.
yourTurn.why: *Recién* plus the participle, matching *café*, which is masculine.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it plural: *El apartamento está recién pintado.* Say: The apartments have just been painted.

pitfalls.why: Almost. The participle matches the noun: *cocina* is feminine, so *pintada*.
Almost. To say you just arrived, use the past: *recién llegué*.

personal: Say one thing you did just now or very recently, starting with *Recién…* (for example *Recién llegué* or *Recién comí*).
